# PayStage — Safety tools for AI agent payments

PayStage is a safety layer for AI agent payments. It sits in front of an agent's wallet and
answers one question before money moves: should this payment happen? Preflight checks return
`pay`, `review`, or `do_not_pay`.

Site: https://paystage.xyz/
GitHub: https://github.com/base-buzz/paystage
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@paystage/preflight
MCP server manifest: https://paystage.xyz/server.json

## Status

- Tool #1 — MCP payment preflight (`@paystage/preflight`): **Available now** — published on npm.
- All other tools: **Roadmap** (outstanding-auth watch is next).

## Tool #1 — MCP payment preflight (Available now)

An MCP server that evaluates a proposed x402 payment against a local policy file and returns
a verdict before the agent signs anything.

### Install

    npx @paystage/preflight

Non-interactive variant:

    npx -y @paystage/preflight

Links:
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@paystage/preflight
- GitHub: https://github.com/base-buzz/paystage

### Policy

One `policy.json` per agent. Example:

    {
      "maxPerCall": "0.05",
      "maxPerDay": "1.00",
      "asset": "USDC",
      "network": "base",
      "payees": {
        "allow": ["0xabc...123"],
        "review": ["*"]
      }
    }

### Verdicts

- `pay` — payment matches policy; safe to sign.
- `review` — payment is ambiguous or unknown; escalate to a human or a higher-level check.
- `do_not_pay` — payment violates policy; do not sign.

## Roadmap

- Outstanding-auth watch — **next**. Detect authorized-but-unsettled payments before an agent double-pays.
- Farcaster approve mini-app — approve or reject pending agent payments from a phone.
- Dead-seller watch — flag payees that stop settling and escalate new payments to review.
- MCP listing provenance receipt — signed receipts tying MCP listings to their source.
- Micro-escrow — small-value escrow for agent-to-agent payments.
- Publish-and-register one-shot — publish an MCP server and register it with a provenance receipt in one command.
